### D0 · Start

**Environment (Nov 7 2026, this VM):** 4 CPUs, 15 GB RAM, 28 GB disk free. Node v22.23.4, npm 10.9.9, Python 3.13.18. Playwright 1.63.0 with Chromium 1243 in `/opt/pw-browsers`; WebKit 2359 (WebKit 26.6) and its system libraries installed by D0 at that same Playwright version (`npx playwright@1.63.0 install webkit`, `install-deps webkit`), and launched headless as an iPhone 14: WebGL 2 answered yes and `createImageBitmap` decoded a WebP there, which the e2e projects do not rely on for the live 3D (Part 2, Testing). `bpy` 5.2.2 LTS, pymupdf, scipy, scikit-image, OpenCV 5.0.0 (contrib, headless), jsonschema, cairosvg and pillow-avif installed by D0 (`pip install --break-system-packages`), about 4 minutes. No `/usr/bin/time`, no `blender` binary (bpy is the renderer). GitHub access through the session's tools works for `FastCoempany/darkestshadeswebsite` (admin); the `darkestshades` release repo is not attached to the session.

**The tortoise textures (F01, F02):** `frame_texture.py` reads `work/out/<shot>/cutout.png`, `layers/lens.png` and `stage-full.png`, which this VM does not have. Rebuilding them here would need `zipget.py` (a GitHub token for the `darkestshades` release, which this session's GitHub access does not cover) and `clean_lightbox.py` (rembg's ISNet and SAM models from Hugging Face, and the whole clean-up per shot). Not done: the DAM holds the same cleaned outputs at full resolution (`dam/product/DS-F01-A1-v01-master.png` is the cut-out with the lens filter in its alpha, `…-stage.png` the stage version), so D0 adds `--from-dam` to `frame_texture.py`, which reads those two files and takes the lens openings from the drawing after the same registration. Run on this VM: `frame_texture.py F02 --from-dam` (13.5 s; outline IoU 0.979; gold 2991 px, onyx 4224 px, pins 2107 px found on the front) and `F01 --from-dam --temples` (13.9 s; IoU 0.971; blue coverage 0.20, the temple band laid). Previews checked by eye: F02's crimson tortoise with the GCD on the right wing and the pins on the left; F01's blue blotches on black. Default behaviour (from `work/out/`) unchanged.

**Spikes:**

- **S4 · CDP touch drag in Chromium:** pass. `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` (touchStart, 12 touchMoves, touchEnd) through a Playwright CDP session, Chromium as a Pixel 7. On a `touch-action: none` pad: 1 pointerdown, 12 pointermoves following the finger (y 177 → 360 px), 1 pointerup. On a `touch-action: pan-y` box: the page scrolled 0 → 568 px, the element saw 1 pointermove then a pointercancel. So the e2e suites can drag with CDP and can tell a drag from a native scroll.
- **S3 · one drawer-view frame at final settings:** the prototype drawer (`drawer_scene.py`, F09 inside, the drawer 250 mm out) at 1200 × 1500, 48 samples, denoised, Cycles on 4 CPUs at `nice 19`: **158 s wall** (`spikes/s3-render.log`: the command and Blender's log), of which about 34 s is building F09 from its drawings (the same build timed in S1's log) and so about 125 s the render. Peak memory not measured (no `/usr/bin/time`). **Queue estimate from it:** base sequence 24 × 125 s ≈ 50 min; eight frame sequences as region renders (about a third of the pixels) 8 × 24 × 45 s ≈ 2.4 h; the two wall plates lit and dark (1170 and 2880 px wide, about 2.5× a sequence frame each) plus three knob close-ups ≈ 40 min; lifted stills and the environment map ≈ 20 min. About 4 h in all, well under the 12 h limit, so both the 720 px and the 1200 px sets are made in run 1.
- **S1 · F09 as a GLB next to Cycles:** done (`docs/build/drawer-wall/spikes/s1_blender.py`, `s1-three.html`, `s1-render.mjs`, `s1-compare.py`; the side-by-side `s1-f09-cycles-vs-three.jpg`: Cycles, three.js, the difference ×4). F09 built with `frame3d`, its Cycles materials swapped for glTF ones (acetate: base near black, roughness 0.06, IOR 1.49; lens: base near black, roughness 0, alpha = 1 − mean transmission, blended; `gcd_gold` metallic, roughness 0.22; `gcd_onyx`), triangulated and decimated (the GCD gently, to a sixth of the budget), exported with Blender's glTF exporter (Y-up, WebP images). Both renderers lit by the same environment: an equirectangular Cycles render of three emissive panels from the frame's centre (1024 × 512, saved as `.hdr`), the Cycles still film-transparent, AgX in both, the same camera (three-quarter from the GCD's side, 100 mm, 1024 px). Numbers, mean absolute difference in 8-bit sRGB over the pixels where either image is brighter than 5/255: as built (5.42 M triangles, decimated to 59,990, GLB 1.20 MB, export 49 s) **31.6**; built at `mesh_step` 4 (0.97 M triangles, decimated to 59,990, GLB 1.26 MB, build 10 s, export 5 s) **24.6**; over the whole image 0.32. three.js is brighter over those pixels (mean luminance 39 against Cycles's 22, out of 255), and by eye the extra light sits along the rims: the decimated mesh's normals scatter the panels' reflections where Cycles's smooth surface shows one thin highlight. Build times: 34 s for F09 as built, 10 s at `mesh_step` 4 (`spikes/s1-blender.log`). The environment's orientation was checked by brute force (`spikes/s1-sweep.sh`: four rotations, mirrored or not): the map as saved, unrotated, is the best. GLB load in three.js 25 ms; WebGL 2 through SwiftShader in headless Chromium. **What D4 takes from it:** build for the GLB at `mesh_step` 4 and decimate less brutally (the triangle budget holds either way); keep smooth normals; the lens as an alpha-blended glossy surface reads right at this size; the match is close enough to go on, and the materials are tuned against the drawer's own HDR before D5 (the risk table). The GLB's `KHR_materials_ior` was not written (1.49 rounds to glTF's default 1.5), so no extension is needed.
- **S2 · a test Artifact (page, module, GLB, WebP):** published, private: https://claude.ai/artifact/2vxLcc1s6j223jMUt8YfSx (`spikes/s2-index.html`, `s2-probe.js`). Six files served with their types: `index.html`, `probe.js` (text/javascript), `still.webp` (image/webp, 15 KB), `still.avif` (image/avif, 12 KB), `data.json`, and the GLB. **The host serves no `.glb`, `.hdr`, `.exr` or `.bin` under any content type** (the served types: html, css, js, mjs, wasm, json, map, txt, md, csv, xml, svg, png, jpg, gif, webp, avif, ico, woff, woff2, ttf, otf, mp3, wav, ogg, mp4, webm, pdf), so the GLB went up as `F09.glb.wasm` (application/wasm, 1.2 MB) and the page fetches it as bytes. From this VM the link answers "Sign in to view this page" (private, as intended), so the runtime half is reported by the page itself: a status line "Pass" or "Fail" followed by module, GLB fetch, WebP decode, AVIF decode and WebGL 2, each yes or no (Pass needs the first three; AVIF and WebGL 2 have fallbacks in the wall), and the full report under a copy button; Antaeus confirms it on a phone (question below). The publication plan for D7 follows from this: the built wall's binary assets that the host will not serve by their own names (the GLBs, the HDR) are published under a served name and loaded as bytes, recorded in the manifest; everything else keeps its name.

### D1 · The project

**The stack, pinned** (`wall/package.json`, all devDependencies, exact versions): vite 8.3.6, typescript 7.0.2 (type-checks the Lit decorators with `experimentalDecorators`), lit 3.3.3, three 0.187.0, @use-gesture/vanilla 10.3.1, @fontsource-variable/mona-sans and urbanist 5.3.0, vitest 5.1.0, @playwright/test 1.63.0 with playwright and playwright-core 1.63.0 (the VM's Chromium 1243 and WebKit 2359 belong to that version; @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0 then shares it), lighthouse 13.6.0 with chrome-launcher 1.2.3, @gltf-transform/{cli,core,functions,extensions} 4.5.1, meshoptimizer 1.3.0, ajv 8.20.0, ajv-formats 3.0.1, @types/three, @types/node.

**What's there:** the scripts (`dev`, `build` = type-check then `vite build` to `wall/dist/` with relative paths and `noindex`, `preview`, `test`, `test:e2e` with `--trace off`, `check`, `lighthouse`, `assets`, `all`); `vite.config.ts` (two pages, three.js in its own chunk, `virtual:fonts-local` for licensed font files in `brand/fonts/private/`, `PUBLIC_ADOBE_FONTS_KIT` for a kit); `playwright.config.ts` with the three projects (wall-pixel: Chromium as a Pixel 7; wall-iphone: WebKit as an iPhone 14; wall-desktop: Chromium at 1440 × 900) against the built wall served by `vite preview`, baselines next to the specs, `WALL_NO_PIXELS=1` for CI; the checks (`checks/strings.mjs`: the banned names over `wall/src`, the pages, `wall/data` and the copy deck's `wall` section; `colors.mjs`: no hex, color functions or named colors in any CSS the wall ships; `schema.mjs`: the records and the manifest against their schemas, a data file without a schema fails; `assets.mjs`: every manifest entry on disk, every file in the manifest, every file within its kind's budget; `lighthouse.mjs`: mobile, performance ≥ 90, LCP ≤ 2.5 s, CLS ≤ 0.1, TBT ≤ 200 ms, the report to `test-results/lighthouse.json`); the empty asset manifest and its schema (kinds, statuses, budgets); `index.html` and `states.html` with labelled placeholders where the wall and the sheet will be, the brand mark as favicon, `noindex`, the scene black; `src/styles/base.css` (the tokens, type that recedes, the focus ring, `.visually-hidden`), `fonts.css` (the stand-ins); the e2e specs `fonts.spec.ts` (each role's faces loaded at its weights, in all three browsers), `pages.spec.ts` (both pages load without errors, carry `noindex`, sit on black, pass axe at WCAG 2.2 AA tags) and `screens.spec.ts` (both pages at 390 and 1440, to `test-results/screens-*/`); `.github/workflows/wall.yml` running `npm run all` without pixel comparisons.

**The token:** `surface-scene` (black) added through `tools/palette.py` in both themes, with `text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-tertiary` (4.5:1) and `focus-ring` (3:1) checked on it in night, the theme the wall renders in (`CHECKS` entries may now name their themes; the paper theme never shows the wall), then `python3 tools/build_tokens.py` (`design/tokens/build/*.css` regenerated; wire mode maps it to white). Contrast report: 16.56, 8.52, 6.08 and 8.85.

**The review's fixes** (an agent that did not build it, against the docs): the colors check now reads every string and numeric literal in the TypeScript too (a three.js `Color('#…')`, a canvas `fillStyle`, `0xffffff`), `.svg` files under `src`, every attribute in the pages, and ties the pages' `theme-color` meta to the `surface-scene` token's built value; named colors count only in CSS and markup, so a knob style called `gold` in the records is not a color. The WebP allowance is gone: AVIF and WebP meet the same budget. `WALL_NO_PIXELS` is wired to Playwright's `ignoreSnapshots` and to nothing else. Lighthouse fails when a metric is missing. The banned-strings patterns take any punctuation between their parts, and the check also reads the manifest, `wall/public` and a built `wall/dist`. Route B for the licensed fonts (files in `brand/fonts/private/`) now injects the `@font-face` rules into each page's head, serves the files in dev and copies them to `dist/fonts/` with relative URLs.

**Exit evidence (Nov 7 2026, rerun after the review's fixes, the D2 drafts out of the tree):** `cd wall && npm run all` → exit 0: strings 15 files, 0 banned; colors 7 files, 0 literal; schema: `assets/manifest.json` validates, `data/wall.json` not there yet (D2); assets 0 entries, 0 failures; Vitest 2 passed; build 100 ms (initial JS 0.05 kB + 0.67 kB, no three.js chunk yet, fonts 189 kB of woff2); Playwright 30 tests: 22 passed, 8 skipped (the review screens run once, from desktop Chromium); Lighthouse mobile performance 100, LCP 752 ms, CLS 0.000, TBT 0 ms. Screens of `index.html` and `states.html` at 390 and 1440 taken by `screens.spec.ts` and shown in the session (stand-in type: Urbanist for the micro labels).

### D2 · Records and logic

**The records** (`wall/data/wall.json`, `wall.schema.json`): nine metaobject-shaped records, one `bay_wall` (handle `frames`; `bays` a JSON list of the eight `drawer_bay` ids in look-number order F01, F02, F03, F04, F05, F06, F08, F09; `knob_style` `black-relief`; `render_set` `wall-v1`) and eight `drawer_bay` (`frame`, `state` `available`, `light` `auto`, `note` empty). The schema holds the field keys, the Shopify field types and the value enums; `npm run check` now requires both data files and fails without them.

**The logic** (`wall/src/`): `data/adapter.ts` (`readRecords`: metaobject shape in, typed drawers out; a missing field null, an unknown value kept for the resolver, a broken `bays` reference or a duplicate reported; `withRecord` replaces one drawer and no other); `lib/resolve.ts` (the seven rules of "How a drawer's state is resolved", `priceText` from the record's amount and currency, `resolveWall`); `lib/machine.ts` (the reducer: every transition of the table, impossible ones return the same object, Esc stepping back, the knob pull carried as a pointer, `RECORD` mid-view); `lib/gestures.ts` (every constant of the table and the pure math: tap, rubber band, pull position, release, turn, inertia, zoom); `lib/spring.ts` (the settle spring at 180/26 in 16 ms substeps); `lib/tier.ts` (tier 1 or 2 from WebGL 2, device memory, Save-Data, a lost context); `lib/manifest.ts` (the asset index: plate, rects, dark crops, sequences per width, GLB, stills, env, cameras, tints; `hasSequence` and `hasLift` for the resolver); `lib/types.ts`; `data/extract.ts` with `virtual:wall-frames` and `virtual:wall-copy` in `vite.config.ts`, so the built wall ships only the eight frames' facts (id, handle, look number, name, descriptor, price, GCD length and placement, front width, lens color) and the copy deck's `wall` section with the alt phrases and the brand's names, nothing of the site's sections.

**The copy** (`content/copy/en.json`, `wall`, status `draft`): the strings DRAWER-WALL.md lists, plus `announce.photo`, the records panel's labels (`panel.*`, "Records (example data)" as Part 1 names it) and the event log's two (`debug.*`); all on the sign-off list below.

**The review's fixes** (an agent that did not build it): the records schema moved to draft 2020-12 so each record carries each key exactly once (`contains` with `minContains`/`maxContains`), `reference` is allowed on a field as the Storefront API returns it, and `checks/schema.mjs` cross-checks the records after validation (every id a `bays` list names is a `drawer_bay`, none twice, every `frame` is a product in `content/products/`). The shipped frame facts are trimmed to what the wall shows (id, handle, look number, name, price): the GCD placement notes, measurements, lens color and descriptor no longer ship, and a value the record lacks is null, never filled in (the handle fallback is gone). Four resolver tests added (locked with no price, sold out without lift assets, hidden with an unknown frame, null name and look number).

**What the run added beyond Part 2's table, kept and recorded** (decision log): a `DRAG` in `opening` or `shutting` catches the settling drawer (Part 1 step 3: the drawer follows a dragging finger); `SHUT_DRAWER`, the quiet button's reverse of `OPEN_DRAWER` (Part 1: `wall.shut`); Esc while pulling settles the drawer shut; Esc during a transition (`entering`, `opening`, `shutting`, `lifting`, `returning`, `leaving`) does nothing, so D5's elements must always emit the completion event; `canLift` turning false while a frame is lifted leaves the view where it is (the doc closes the view only when the drawer can no longer open); `priceText` formats a non-USD price as "EUR 100" and shows cents only when there are any (the records hold $100, so neither case is reached). The resolver and the adapter return their problems; `log.ts` (D5) writes them to the debug log, so "and logged" lands with the elements.

### D3 · The wall and the drawer

**The tools:** `tools/blender/drawer_wall.py` (the cabinet and the drawers from the prototype: calfskin grain anchored to each drawer's parts so no two drawers match and a sliding front keeps its grain, piping, the knob tilted 28° with the 30 mm GCD as black relief, gold or plain; the seam light as state, a warm pool of light on the suede inside; the two layouts, orthographic 15° down with the cabinet's face and top centred in a black room, `rects.json` projected from the geometry; the 24-frame drawer-view sequence with the camera moving from the wall's angle to looking in, region renders for a frame; the knob close-ups; `cameras`, which places every frame where the render put it and writes its lifted pose; `env`; `lifted`; `check`, which holds the rects to the geometry and the knob rect to the knob's own projected vertices, the dark crops to the plate, the edges to scene black, the knob GCD to 30 mm, and the camera files to the render's camera), `tools/photo/grade_scene.py` (the prototype's grade as the one grade and the default, grain seeded per output, an exact-black edge band per kind), `tools/blender/render_queue.py` (resumable jobs in chunks; outputs verified and required to be newer than the job's start; only a run stamps a job, with the tool code as it stood when the job began; `add` keeps an unchanged job's record and marks a changed one for re-rendering; outputs the queue did not make are `adopted`), `tools/blender/wall_export.py` (the web outputs within budget, the dark crops with the plate's own grain, the manifest entries with the queue's exact commands and the edge measurement, `stills`, `knobs`, `r1`), `tools/blender/queue_d3.sh`.

**Lookdev** (`work/wall/lookdev*.png`, against `prototype/stills/`): the room's light brought down to the prototype's level; the seam glow as a thin amber line; the drawer's suede darkened to brown-black with a warm pool on its floor; the view's end pose moved back so the cabinet shows above the open drawer. The grade measured against the founder-reviewed still: its cabinet sits at about 36/255, so the wall's grade is the cool cast at exposure 0.3 with a 0.004 toe (the leather lands at 38/255); one grade for every image, the drawer's warmth from the scene's own light so the view continues the wall at its first frame. The portrait rail went from 96 to 114 mm after the first wall build showed a two-line name pushing its price into the drawer below at 390 px; the landscape rail from 56 to 76 mm after the second review measured its label at 43 px at 1024 px wide, where the longest name (28 characters) wraps to two lines and the stack of number, name and price needs about 58. In the finished walls the third column's knobs catch the room's overhead light more than the others (at a 720 px test the knobs' mean levels run 32 to 70 of 255; the small glint light makes little difference, the broad light above does): that is the room's light mirrored in tilted metal, and it is left for R1's answer on the room.

**The D3 review and its fixes (Nov 7 2026):** an agent that did not build D3 reviewed the branch and found, in order of weight: (1) `camera/open.json` and `inspect.json` placed the frame about 79 mm deeper and 24 mm higher than the render, so the live frame would not have started where the rendered one lay, and the lifted still showed the frame off-centre and nearly black; (2) the grade's edge mask (black to 3.5%, full at 7.5% of each dimension) reached into the top row's drawers, and the plate's top band held the cabinet's tilted top, so "scene black is exact" was met by a mask, not by the scene; (3) the world-space grain crawled across a sliding front over the 250 mm of the drawer view; (4) base frames 0 to 4 and the plain knob close-up predated the rail change, which the queue could not notice; (5) the queue took any non-empty file as a finished output; (6) the check skipped silently without the renders and sampled only the lit plate; (7) the manifest's `sourceCommit` was always one commit behind, its commands lacked their flags; (8) the grade's defaults were the prototype's, not the wall's; (9) the dev server's path guard lacked a separator. Everything was fixed in `2b253f0`: the cameras use build_drawer's own arithmetic for every frame, with each frame's bounds, and the lifted pose was remade (turned 35° about the frame's centre, leaned back to face the camera 8° short of its angle, 130 mm up and 120 mm toward it, the lenses transparent so the drawer shows through, the key 12 W); the plate frames the whole cabinet with 3.27% of its width as room on every side and the band is 2% black (never narrower than 32 px, two WebP macroblocks, after the 720 px frame 16 kept 4/255 of encoder ringing in the sampled band at any quality) and full from 3.2% of the width, which the check now measures on the renders themselves and on every web output; the grain is anchored (a part's world position less its `slide`); the whole base sequence, the plain knob, the cameras and the lifted still were re-rendered after the fixes, and the four walls after the re-framing; the queue verifies outputs, redoes a done job whose output has gone and names jobs rendered with other tool code; the manifest carries `-dirty` when the tools had uncommitted changes, a `toolsHash` of the tool files, the queue's exact commands and the edge measurement; the grade's defaults are the wall's. The drawer view's frames keep a wider fade (2% to 6% of the width): a vignette into the page's black, as the prototype had, recorded in the decision log.

**The second review and its fixes (Nov 8 2026):** a second agent that did not build D3 reviewed the branch through four lenses (the geometry, the checks, the brand and the documents, reproducibility), and each of its twelve heaviest findings was put to two further agents to refute. In order of weight: (1) the three.js camera quaternion in `camera/open.json` and `inspect.json` looked 90° away from the render's camera (the conversion conjugated the camera's own axes along with the world's; the frames' matrices were right); (2) the environment map had been captured from the first lifted pose, 92 mm from the remade one, and this file said nothing in it had changed; (3) the lifted still focused on a point 22 mm in the air before the frame's front, at f/4 with 8 mm of depth of field, so the front and the GCD rendered soft (one refuter held the GCD sharp enough; the mechanism stood); (4) the knob rect in `rects.json` tilted the knob down instead of up and sat 22 px (portrait) and 28 px (landscape) below the knob in the plate, which the check could not see because it compared the rects with their own arithmetic; (5) the queue's tool stamp was written at `add` time and overwritten by every refill, so it could not name the code that rendered a job, and `run` adopted outputs it had not made as if it had; (6) the R1 lifted still had been rendered with the tool's default lens tint, not F09's measured one, because the queue's record kept the command from before `queue_d3.sh` gained the flag; (7) the suede lining's nap was still read in world space and crawled across the sliding box, as the calfskin's grain had before the first review; (8) the landscape rail (56 mm) gave the label 43 px at 1024 px wide, where the longest name wraps to two lines; (9) a D4 decision-log row named the knob's GCD where it meant the frame's, and departed from DRAWER-WALL.md's "the GCD stays at full detail" without saying so; (10) three numbers in the queue paragraph did not match the logs, and `status` named 33 stale jobs, not 32; (11) the check's verdict read "0 failures" and exit 0 with four measurements skipped (both refuters held this to be no defect against the documents; it is changed all the same); (12) the asset check sized each budget from the manifest's width without reading the file. Noted besides: the WebP quality was not in the manifest, the environment map's orientation was not recorded, and the knob style is verified on the geometry the check rebuilds rather than on the plate's pixels. The tools were fixed in `316dddc`: the quaternion is R q, with a guard in `write_cameras` and a check part that reads both camera files; the suede subtracts `slide` like the calfskin and the box's floor, sides and back carry it; the knob rect turns the pivot's way, and the check projects every vertex of each knob and its GCD and holds the rect to them within 0.15% of the plate; the lifted still focuses between the GCD's median depth and the front's centre, measured along the camera's axis, at f/8 (the GCD then sits 9 mm before the focus and the front's centre 13 mm behind it, about 1.3 and 1.9 px of blur at 1200 px; the far temple falls off as before); the landscape rail is 76 mm; the queue's `add` keeps an unchanged job and marks a changed one `rerun`, `run` alone writes the stamp and marks outputs it did not make `adopted`, and `status` names stale, adopted, unstamped and rerun jobs; the check's verdict counts skipped measurements and exits 2 on any; the asset check reads every AVIF's and WebP's size from its header; the manifest records the WebP quality, the crops' qualities and the environment map's capture point and orientation. Then the renders: the landscape walls (the rail), the three knob close-ups, the whole base sequence, the cameras, the environment map and F09's lifted still (with its measured tint) were rendered again with the fixed tools, each job stamped as it ran; the two portrait walls were kept, their records carried into `d3.json` from the `d3w` queue that rendered them (stamp `879c900d5308`, commit `2b253f0`'s tool files; nothing a wall render uses has changed since: on a shut drawer the suede subtracts a zero `slide`, the rail change is the landscape's, and the rest touch the lifted still, the cameras and the check). The earlier record is kept on this machine as `work/queue/d3.before-review2.json`. The D4 region renders made before the suede fix (48 of 176) were discarded; D4 starts its queue afresh. What the check still cannot see: the knob's style on the plate itself (the export takes each plate from the render named for its layout and knob, and the manifest records that command), and the drawer view's frames meet scene black at their edges by the grade's band, not by the scene (their raw renders reach 188/255 there, because the open drawer fills the view), which is the recorded vignette decision, put to R1.

### D5 · The elements

**The shared pieces** (`wall/src/lib/`, written first in one context in the D3 and D4 windows on the worktree branch `wip/d5-prep`, brought in with `48e4628` and finished here): `sequence-player.ts` (the drawer view's frames fetched as encoded blobs, about 1 MB a drawer at 720 px; decoded bitmaps kept only for the current frame ± 2 and closed otherwise, the next ones decoded ahead in the direction of travel; a cross-fade between neighbours on a 2D canvas sized to the view at the device pixel ratio; AVIF where `createImageBitmap` takes it, WebP otherwise; the first and last frames load first; the decoding and the canvas injectable for the tests), `scroll-lock.ts` (the body fixed at its scroll position while the view is open, the only lock Safari honours, restored on release), `focus-trap.ts` (Tab cycles inside the dialog, focus starts on the first control and goes back to the drawer on release; the root may live in a shadow tree and the controls in nested shadow trees, the photographs' bar and the live frame's canvas among them, so the focusable list is collected through open shadow roots in tree order, the active element is read down through them and a focus event's target comes from its composed path; the D5 review found the first version stopping at the root's own tree, below), `copy.ts` (every string from the deck's wall section through one function with its placeholders filled; a key the deck lacks returns an empty string and is reported once, so a missing string renders nothing), `log.ts` (the in-memory event log behind `?debug=1`, mirrored to the console; nothing is kept without the flag). `wall/src/data/store.ts`: the records through the adapter, the manifest through its index, the frames' facts, every drawer resolved; one `change` event names the drawers whose resolution changed, so each bay re-renders on its own.

**The elements** (`wall/src/elements/`): `<drawer-wall>` lays the bays over the wall plate from the `bay_wall` record (portrait under 1024 px, landscape from 1024; the plate is the LCP element with a fixed aspect from `rects.json`; the page's only heading visually hidden; a polite live region for the announcements). `<drawer-bay>`: one drawer, its resolved state, its label, its dark crop, its events; the face a button named "{name}, $100. Open the drawer." (a locked one "Not yet. $100", `aria-disabled` so it stays in the Tab order and is announced); a hidden drawer renders no control; the sold-out word in `text-secondary`, which holds 4.5:1 over the rail's pixels; tap first (a tap on the face opens, the wall scrolls natively) or pull first (the knob's rect takes the pull with the pointer carried, the rest of the face scrolls). `<drawer-view>`: the full-screen view as one dialog over the wall (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, named for the frame; nothing behind it scrolls); the shut drawer barely lit with the pull hint; pull down to scrub the sequence; let go and it settles open or shut (velocity first, then position; a full pull is 45% of the view's height); quiet buttons do the same, and the lifted view's buttons cover every gesture (turn left and right, tilt up and down, closer, further, reset); a tap on the frame's region of the stage lifts it (a finger that has not moved 8 px is still a tap), "Lift them out" does the same for the keyboard and assistive technology; the photographs open over the view; put back, shut, close with focus back on the drawer; the name and $100 stay on screen; reduced motion cross-fades at about 160 ms and the drawer snaps; a 10 ms haptic tick at the stops where `navigator.vibrate` exists. `<lifted-frame>`: the live frame, three.js loaded at the first tier-2 lift (its named pieces through `lifted-three.ts`, their own chunk) and never in the initial bundle nor at tier 1; one canvas rendered only while something changes, AgX, the drawer's own HDR as the environment plus one warm key; the handoff mounts the GLB at `open.json`'s transform over the drawer's last frame with a soft contact shadow and cross-fades over 120 ms while the drawer behind it cross-fades to the base sequence's last frame, the empty drawer (`lifted-handoff` tells the view when the frame fades in and out), then springs to the inspect pose; turning, pinching and the wheel report deltas up to the view, whose machine holds the pose; tier 1 shows the lifted still instead; a lost context means tier 1 for the rest of the visit. `<photo-zoom>`: the real lightbox photographs (A1, A2, A3 and A6 where they exist) on their stage colour at full resolution; pinch, drag or double-tap to one image pixel per screen pixel, drag and the wheel on desktop, keys + − 0 and the arrows, and while the photograph is larger than the view the bar's Up, Down, Left and Right buttons move it by half a view (the drag's button); the only place the pale stage appears; with no entries for the frame it renders only the bar with "Back to the frame". `<records-panel>`: the simulated backend behind `?panel=1`, labelled "Records (example data)": any drawer's frame, state and light changed in the in-memory records through the store's `update()`, and only that drawer changes; the `?mech=` choice sits here too. `states.html` (`states.ts`): every element in every state from fixtures: the eight bay fixtures (available lit, sold out dark, locked, hidden, light forced dark, light forced lit, no frame, an unknown state; the last two hidden and logged), the pull-first bay, a bay at 320 px; the portrait and the landscape wall from the records; the view shut, pulling, open, lifted, turned, zoomed, the photographs, tier 1 lifted, reduced motion; the records panel; the resolver's log. The sheet prepares its fixtures together, decodes every image under it and then sets `window.__states.ready`, which the screenshot test waits for.

**Found and fixed while building (Nov 8 2026):** (1) the environment map's rotation: Blender's equirectangular capture puts forward (+y) at u = 0.5 and the camera's right (+x) at u = 0.75 (checked with a probe map, red at the camera's right, green up, blue ahead), so in three.js `scene.environmentRotation = Euler(0, +π/2, 0)` puts the capture in its own directions; −π/2 was exactly reversed (ahead behind, right left); `ENV_ROTATION_Y = Math.PI / 2`, and the env entry of the manifest records it as `threeRotation`. (2) The frame's tap target: the stage captured the pointer on pointerdown, so a pointer click on the invisible "Lift them out" button over the frame never lifted (only the keyboard reached it); the dialog then held two controls with the same name. Now the stage's pointer-up lifts on a tap inside the frame's region (22–78% across, 30–54% down, the box the button had), and the one visible "Lift them out" button serves the keyboard and assistive technology (every gesture has a button that does the same). (3) The pull-first knob: `drawer-bay.knobStyle()` grew the knob to 44 px as a percentage of the plate's size and took an unknown size as 1 px, so until the size arrived the knob was 4400% of the bay: it covered the wall, the mobile browser zoomed out to fit an 18 000 px layout, and a swipe on F03's face landed on F09's knob; and the size never arrived in `index.html`, because the wall attached its ResizeObserver in `firstUpdated`, before the store (set after the first render) had drawn the plate; the states sheet sets the store first and never showed it. The knob keeps its drawn rect until the plate's size is known, and the wall observes the plate from the first update that renders it. (4) The canvases on a size change: `lifted-frame.resize()` ran once at setup, so a phone turned while the frame is lifted kept the old canvas size; the host is observed with a ResizeObserver from `setup()` (disconnected in `dispose()`) and a size change resizes the renderer and draws again; the drawer view draws again when its canvas's size changes while the drawer rests open (observed from `enter`, disconnected in `leave`). Not yet run on a device: D7's checklist (turn the phone while open and while lifted) is the test. (5) The photographs' empty case rendered the "See the photographs" string as its empty state; it renders nothing but the bar now (a missing value renders nothing). D6 decides whether the button hides when the zoom index lacks the frame (the resolver does not know the index, a runtime file never committed). (6) The `?debug=1` copy button sat over the view's bottom controls at 412 px (z-index 30); now 5, under the view (10) and the panel (20). (7) The focus trap through shadow roots, as above. (8) The states baselines (found on this branch, Nov 8): the drafts' baselines came from the worktree, where the sheet had shown the base sequence in the open fixtures and no lifted still (the F09 assets had not been there when they were written); on this branch `--update-snapshots` kept them, because Playwright rewrites a baseline only when the comparison fails, and with pixelmatch's default colour threshold (0.2) a black frame on the dark suede and a dark still over the dark drawer did not count as a difference within the 0.2% of the page the config allowed (`maxDiffPixelRatio` 0.002). Found by looking at the baseline (the open drawer empty, the tier-1 view without its still). The comparison is now tight (`threshold: 0.1`, at most 200 differing pixels, the live canvases masked), the baselines were deleted and written again, three runs match them, and the old frameless baseline fails against the sheet by 33 900 pixels. (9) The `?open=` flow asserted the frame's name on the `drawer-view` host's `aria-label`; the dialog is the view's own `.view` element since the dialog change, so the test now asserts the dialog's accessible name (`getByRole('dialog', { name })`); the behaviour was right, the test was stale (it had never run with F08's sequence).

**The D5 review and its fixes (Nov 9 2026):** four reviewers who did not build the branch read it through the mechanics, the tests, the brand and accessibility, and reproducibility; every finding was then put to two agents told to refute it. Thirty findings, twelve verified (none refuted), eighteen lighter ones returned unverified; all twelve fixed here, with the unverified ones that were cheap and right. (1) **The lift never reached the live frame in the wall.** `drawer-view.lift()` queried `<lifted-frame>` synchronously inside the dispatch that requests the render which mounts it, found nothing, and fell back to a 900 ms timer: the machine reached `lifted` while the live frame and the still stayed at opacity 0 (the states sheet hid it, because its fixtures call `lift()` after `updateComplete`; the lift flow asserted the machine's state and yaw only). `lift()` and `putBack()` now wait for the update first; the lift flow asserts the live canvas at opacity 1 and the frame's progress at 1, the WebGL-disabled flow lifts and asserts the still. (2) **Tier 1 never defined `<lifted-frame>`** (`main.ts` imported it at tier 2 only), so no lifted still could show in `index.html`; the element loads at every tier now, and three.js only inside its tier-2 setup through `lifted-three.ts` (a dynamic `import('three')` would carry the whole library, 819 kB against 647, because a namespace object cannot be tree-shaken). (3) **The focus trap stopped at the dialog's own tree:** `querySelectorAll` does not enter shadow roots, so in the photographs state the Tab cycle was empty and every Tab parked on the dialog root, and in the lifted state the live frame's canvas was skipped; the trap collects focusables through open shadow roots in tree order and reads the active element down through them; a keyboard flow Tabs through the lifted view's cycle (the canvas, the buttons, the canvas again) and the photographs' bar. (4) **Two gestures had no button:** the vertical drag that tilts the lifted frame and the drag that pans a zoomed photograph; six quiet buttons added (`wall.tiltUp`, `wall.tiltDown`; `wall.panUp`, `wall.panDown`, `wall.panLeft`, `wall.panRight`, the last four shown while the photograph is larger than the view), drafts on the sign-off list. (5) **A tap with any movement never lifted:** the first `pointermove` on the open drawer became a pull, so only a motionless tap reached the frame; a finger that has not moved 8 px (the tap slop, `TAP_MAX_PX`) on the open or the shut drawer is still a tap, and the lift flow taps with two pixels of movement. (6) **The full pull measured 45% of the stage's height, not the view's** (219 px instead of 380 at 390 × 844; the constant and DRAWER-WALL.md say the view); the view's height now, and the Pixel flow holds a drag at 45% of the stage's height (not open) and then at 45% of the view's (open). (7) **The rendered frame stayed in the dimmed drawer under the lifted frame** as a ghost; the drawer behind the lift now cross-fades to the base sequence's last frame, the empty drawer (DRAWER-WALL.md, The handoff), in step with the live frame's own fade, and the poster, the canvas and the empty drawer are dimmed as one group. (8) **The reduced-motion test could not tell a snap from the spring** (the spring settles in about 690 ms, the bound was 700); the bound is 250 ms, the test checks the media query took, and counts the view's draws between the state changes from the event log mirrored to the console: one under reduced motion, about forty for the spring. (9) **The WebGL-disabled test's assertion was vacuous** ("Turn left" absent in the open state, where it never renders at any tier); it lifts now and asserts the still at opacity 1, the live canvas at 0, no turn or tilt buttons, the photographs offered. (10) **The record overstated Vitest's reach** (no test touched the store); `store.test.ts` tests the store against the committed records and manifest (resolution, `update()` naming only the changed drawer, nothing named when nothing changed, the mechanic). (11) **"Sold out" in `text-tertiary` fell under 4.5:1 on the rail** (4.31:1 against the rail's mean luminance, 3.74:1 against its bright grain, measured on the portrait plate's pixels under the label); `text-secondary` now (6.26:1 and 5.42:1). (12) The three full Playwright runs, the two states runs, the check, the build and the asset checks reproduced the exit evidence exactly, and the file set, the pins and the hygiene were as recorded. From the unverified findings: the view announced "The drawer is open." on entry, while the drawer is shut (`wall.announce.entered` now, "{name}. The drawer is shut."); the return from the lift fired the open stop's haptic and announcement a second time (only `announce.back` now); a locked drawer's `disabled` face was out of the Tab order (`aria-disabled`); the records-panel fixture on the sheet rendered inline (the host is `display: block`); the sheet had no landscape wall (it has one); the axe test analysed the sheet before `window.__states.ready` (after it now) and the live-canvas test could pass with no live fixture (it names the three); the keyboard flow's ArrowDown step is asserted by the drawer's position; three skip messages named only Chromium where they mean the Pixel project, and the reduced-motion skip on WebKit is now called the choice it is; the drafts carry their draft line, `main.ts` names its phase D5, and the usability draft's `&debug=1` reads `?debug=1`. Not taken: the 220 px floor on the pull from the prototype (not in the constants); the record's old-allowance figure is corrected below.

**Drafted early, finished in D7:** `docs/build/drawer-wall/usability.md` (the five-person test on their own phones) and `device-checklist.md` (the real-device checklist for R2) came in with the drafts; D7 finishes them against the built wall.

**Known limits, for D6 and D7:** the keyboard flows (`flows.spec.ts`) open, pull with ArrowDown/PageDown, lift, Tab through the lifted view's controls and the photographs' bar, put back, shut and close; turning by the arrow keys while lifted is not yet asserted (D6). At 390 px a two-line name pushes the sold-out word 8.7 px below the label rect onto the next drawer's piping (and under its dark crop when that drawer is dark): D6 decides between the price and the word on one line and a deeper portrait rail. The states baselines depend on `wall/public/zoom/` (git-ignored, from `npm run assets`): on a fresh clone the photographs fixture fails until the folder exists. The sheet's "reduced motion" fixture is the open fixture under that caption (a static sheet cannot set the media query; the flow test covers reduced motion). The photographs' buttons carry the shoot's angle codes (A1, A2, A3, A6) as their text, a question below. One of the review's three full Playwright runs lost Playwright's own preview server mid-run (`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` from the fifth test); not reproduced in the other five runs. A lifted still scaled on a canvas can show an RGB fringe at its transparent pixels (premultiplication); watched for on the device in D7. The e2e runs take the CPU from a render chunk at nice 19; D5's ran after the D4 queue had finished. Playwright's `webServer` reuses a preview server already on port 4173 (`reuseExistingServer` outside CI), so a server left by an earlier probe serves the tests; the dist is read from disk on each request, so the content stays current, but a stale server should be stopped before a run. The iPhone project (WebKit) runs only the flows that need no touch through CDP and no WebGL: every drawer's label, `?open=`, the no-JavaScript list, the records panel and the pages; D6 looks at touch on WebKit through Playwright's own touchscreen.

Skipped: wall-pixel 10 (flows ×2, screens ×4, states ×4); wall-iphone 16 (flows ×8, screens ×4, states ×4); wall-desktop 3 (flows ×3). Each skip names its reason in the spec: the touch flows drive touch through CDP, so they run on the Pixel project only; the live frame and the WebGL flag need Chromium; reduced motion is checked on the Chromium projects by choice; the keyboard flows run on the desktop; the review screens and the states sheet are desktop Chromium at two widths.
- `npm run check` → `strings: 59 files scanned, 0 banned strings`, `colors: 30 files scanned, 0 literal colors`, `assets: 472 entries, 930 files listed, 930 files on disk, 0 failures`, exit 0. `npm run build` → `✓ built in 1.45s`, exit 0; three.js in its own chunk, `three-CPBoSSGV.js` 647.49 kB (163.07 kB gzipped), reached only through `lifted-three-DWAq_lKn.js` (0.44 kB) from `lifted-frame-B7pVkTpL.js` (11.36 kB) at a tier-2 lift; the entry `index-DHuNb477.js` 4.00 kB (1.68 kB gzipped); `dist/index.html` and `dist/states.html` name no three chunk.

### D6 · The wall, together

**What runs from `index.html`** (`wall/src/main.ts`, carried from D5 and finished here): the store from the records and the manifest; the tier chosen from the signals at start (`data-tier` on the wall; `window.__wall` carries the store and the tier for the tests and the usability sessions' console); `?mech=pull` for the pull-first mechanic; `?panel=1` for the records panel; `?open=` (an id or a handle) for the deep link to a drawer on its last frame, not lifted; `?debug=1` for the event log and its copy button; the drawer view, the photographs and the lifted frame loaded on the first open, never in the initial bundle. **Added in D6:** opening a drawer prefetches the lift's pieces at idle priority (DRAWER-WALL.md, In the browser): at tier 2 the three.js chunk through `lifted-three.ts`, then the frame's GLB and the environment map as low-priority fetches into the HTTP cache, so the lift finds them; nothing at tier 1, where the still is the lift. The view offers "See the photographs" only when the zoom index holds a photograph of the frame (the D5 question: the button hides, a missing value renders nothing; `photosFor()` in `photo-zoom.ts`, read once per visit). A drawer's label puts the price and the sold-out word on one line, so a two-line name at 390 px leaves the label inside its rect (the D5 review's depth finding: the word on its own line overran the rect by 9 px onto the next drawer's piping). The photographs' angle buttons announce the picture as the arrow keys do. The drawer view draws once per animation frame however many pointer events arrive in it (a finger reports up to 120 a second), and skips a draw that would repeat the last position.

**The tests added** (`wall/tests/e2e/`): `a11y.spec.ts`: axe on the wall and on the view shut, open, lifted and in the photographs; the dialog's name, the live frame's name and every live announcement (entered, open, lifted, the photographs by key and by button, back, shut); every control at least 44 px (the quiet buttons in the open and the lifted view, the photographs' bar with the pan buttons, the eight pull-first knobs); 320 px with no horizontal scroll on the wall or in the view, the name and $100 on screen; the labels' contrast against the plate's pixels under each label rect, portrait and landscape (the plate drawn on a canvas, the rect's luminance measured; the three label colours against the rect's mean, with the 95th and 99th percentiles recorded). `perf.spec.ts`: three.js absent from the initial load and fetched only once a drawer is open (the prefetch), from the network log; at most 5 decoded frames held through two full pulls out and back (the debug log's `held`); input to the next frame on open, pull and turn (every pointer event's time to the next animation frame, under 200 ms); the frame rate while pulling and turning, at the machine's own speed and at 4× CPU throttling, from the animation-frame gaps. `flows.spec.ts`: the arrow keys and + − 0 on the lifted frame (the pose from the machine); the view without photographs (the zoom index routed empty: no button); the iPhone project's own taps (WebKit's touchscreen: a tap opens, the quiet buttons pull and shut, the lift shows the still or the live frame as the tier allows, close returns focus). `wall/checks/bundle.mjs` (`npm run budget`, in `npm run all` after the build): the initial JavaScript (every script and modulepreload `dist/index.html` names, gzipped) at most 60 KB with no three.js in it; the 3D chunk at most 200 KB gzipped, statically imported by `lifted-three` alone and named by neither page.

**Found and fixed while building (Nov 9 2026):** (1) **Two draws in flight at a deep link left the wrong frame on the canvas:** `show()` drew the first frame and `jumpOpen()` the last without waiting for each other, so whichever decode finished last won, and with frame 0 winning the drawer sat open on a shut picture; found by the reduced-motion flow once draws skipped a repeated position (the snap to 0 was then "unchanged"). Draws now run one after another, the latest last. (2) **The pull drew once per pointer event:** a finger reports up to 120 moves a second; the view draws once per animation frame now (`requestDraw`) and skips a draw that repeats the last position at the same size. (3) **Tried and taken out again: decoding the frames at the canvas's size.** The frames decode at their encoded size (1200 × 1500, 1.8 Mpx a frame, 36 MB for the five held) and are scaled on every draw; decoding them at the canvas's device size (`createImageBitmap` with `resizeWidth`/`resizeHeight`, 0.85 Mpx and 17 MB for five on the Pixel) made a draw a plain copy but dropped more frames under 4× CPU throttling (slowest frames 66.7, 116.6 and 83.3 ms across three runs, against 33.5 and 50.1 before; 60 fps at 1× either way), so it is out, with the numbers kept here. (4) **The bundle check's first version counted the preload map as an import:** Vite writes the three.js chunk's name into the chunks that import `lifted-three` dynamically (`__vite__mapDeps`), which loads it only when that import runs; the check now looks for a static import (`from "./three-…js"`) and found one, in `lifted-three` alone. (5) **The live-canvas test on the sheet named three live fixtures** where the photographs fixture carries a fourth under the photographs (D5's review run); it names four. (6) **The frame-rate test's first assertion asked the 4× budget of this machine** (below, Known limits): it asserts the floor at the machine's own speed, in absolute terms since the review (the median gap at most 17 ms and no gap over two 60 Hz periods plus a millisecond), and records the 4× figures. (7) **The look number's camel failed the grain.** The label-contrast test's first measure was the 99th percentile of the rail's pixels; camel-500 (`#BF835F`) gave 4.10:1 there on the darkest portrait rail (4.28:1 at the 95th; a fifth of that rect's pixels under 4.5:1), while bone-100 and ash-300 met both percentiles everywhere (10.26 and 5.28 at the 99th). The first fix measured the mean alone (4.67:1 for camel) and put the colour question to Antaeus; the D6 review held that to be a check weakened to pass (WCAG's G18 reads the pixels next to the letters, so the grain counts), rightly. The check now asserts the mean and both percentiles for every label colour, and the look numbers are `camel-400` (`#CB997C`, camel-500 lifted from L 0.56 to 0.64 at its hue and saturation, a new step in `tools/palette.py` for small editorial text over the leather; `text-editorial` on the night theme maps to it): 5.91 / 5.41 / 5.19:1 on the darkest portrait rail and 6.27 / 5.72 / 5.49 landscape at the mean, 95th and 99th percentiles, no pixel under 4.5:1 but the single brightest flecks (4.30:1 at the very brightest). Camel-500 stays the brand's camel everywhere else; the question to Antaeus is now whether camel-400 may stay on the wall.

**The D6 review and its fixes (Nov 9 2026):** four reviewers who did not build the branch read it through the measurements, the checks, the brand and the documents, and reproducibility; every finding then went to two refuters. Thirty-three findings, twelve verified, nine stood, three were refuted (that the frame-rate sample counts animation frames rather than canvas draws, which it does by design and now says so; that the suite was not reproducibly green, two connection refusals that the refuters traced to a preview server another run had left on the port; that the bundle check reads only the static graph, which is its job, the runtime side being `perf.spec.ts`'s). The nine, all fixed here: (1) **the label-contrast check** measured the mean so camel-500 passed, three findings from three lenses: the check asserts the mean, the 95th and the 99th percentile now and the look numbers are camel-400 (item 7 above). (2) **At 320 px a two-line label left its rail** by 5.7 px, and with the drawer below set dark its crop painted over the price (the non-negotiable "$100 always visible"; two findings): the label sits above every dark crop (`z-index: 1`), and under 360 px the label's type is 10 px with tighter lines and no gaps, which keeps a two-line name inside the 58.7 px rect with room; the 320 px test measures every label's content against its rect and the next drawer's face, with the records as they are and with the longest name sold out on every drawer, at 320 and at 390. (3) **`checks/lighthouse.mjs` left its preview server orphaned** (`npm run preview` was signalled, not vite; two findings): it spawns vite itself in its own process group and kills the group, refuses to run when something already answers on the port, names the LCP element from Lighthouse 13's insight audits (the plate, `div.plate > picture > img`) and fails if it cannot, and writes its report to `work/lighthouse/` where Playwright's clean-up does not reach it. (4) **The frame-rate floor was relative to the run's own median** (a run slow throughout would have passed): absolute now (item 6). (5) **CI never ran the bundle budget:** `wall.yml` runs `npm run budget` after the build. From the twenty-one lighter findings, the ones taken: the view's axe pass runs on the Pixel project too (it was desktop-only); the bundle check parses the page's tags in any attribute order, requires the entry among them, forbids the three.js chunk's name in any initial file, counts three.js, `lifted-three` and `lifted-frame` together against the 200 KB (lifted-frame-D79YppvW.js + lifted-three-DWAq_lKn.js 4.46 kB: 162.55 kB for the live frame); the decoded-frames test reads the peak as each decode lands as well as the count after each draw (the latter is bounded by construction); the input latency is measured to the frame after the next, past the paint; the lift's prefetch runs once a visit per frame (it re-fetched the GLB on every open); "See the photographs" renders only once the index has answered with a count above 0, and the sheet's fixtures wait for it; Playwright owns its preview server (`reuseExistingServer: false`, its errors shown); the device checklist's "Another" row says what the wall does; the record's environment row carries the final build's 4× figures, the two gzipped sizes are explained (Vite's estimate against zlib's measure, the budget's), and the false sentence that no colour but bone met the 99th percentile is gone. Not taken: a 200% zoom test (the 320 px reflow is WCAG 1.4.10's measure; a text-only zoom test is noted below as not in the suite); the Phases row's pull-request number is filled once the request exists, as every phase has done.

**Known limits, for D7 and run 2:** the frame-rate budget at 4× CPU throttling cannot be verified here: this VM composites in software and shares four CPUs, so at 4× the pull drops frames and the figure varies by run (the slowest frame 33.5 and 50.1 ms in the first two runs, 50.0, 66.6 and 50.0 ms on the build before the review, 66.7 ms after it; the turn held 60 fps in every run but for two single skipped frames, 33.3 ms once at 4× and 33.4 ms once at 1×), while at the machine's own speed pull and turn held 60 fps throughout. The 30 fps at 4× is a Chromium trace on a GPU-composited developer machine (the Budgets table) and is listed under "Checks failing for environment reasons" above; the device checklist (D7) has a smoothness row for the phone. The frame-rate sample counts animation frames (whether the main thread kept up), not canvas draws: in the lab the drawer redraws about 28 times a second because the CDP drag itself paces at that rate, which the test now prints beside the frame figures. Lighthouse's LCP (2257 ms) passes with little room under 2500 ms on this machine (Lighthouse's own mobile throttling over software rendering; the plate is requested only once the module has rendered the shadow tree, 210 ms of resource delay), and TBT varies between runs (53 ms here, 19 to 188 across the review's and this run's readings); run 2 should watch both on a developer machine. `?tier=` to force a tier was not added (the tier is read from the signals and shown as `data-tier`; the WebGL-disabled flow forces tier 1 by removing WebGL). The plan's "320 px and 200% zoom": 320 px is tested as reflow (WCAG 1.4.10's measure, which stands in for 400% zoom at 1280); no text-only 200% zoom test is in the suite. The states baselines were written again twice here, for the sold-out fixtures' one-line row and then for the look numbers in camel-400; they still depend on `wall/public/zoom/`. The iPhone project taps through WebKit's own touchscreen (open, the quiet buttons, the lift at the tier WebKit gives, close); drags stay the Pixel project's through CDP. Turning by the arrow keys is asserted; turning by a drag only on the Pixel. The 220 px floor on the pull from the prototype is still not in the constants. The input-latency figure is to the start of the frame after the next (past the paint), a lab proxy for INP, not a field measure.

### D7 · On a phone

**The phone build and its link** (O18: a private Artifact Antaeus shares): `npm run build` makes `wall/dist/`; `node tools/web/phone_set.mjs` makes the set the Artifact takes from it, in `work/phone/` (never committed): the page without the document skeleton the host adds (the metas, the module script and its preloads, the stylesheet inlined with its font URLs pointed at `./assets/`, `<drawer-wall>` and the `<noscript>` list); the 1200 px sequences in WebP (the host holds at most 511 files in a version, and both widths in both formats are 864; the 720 px set serves low-density screens, AVIF is a saving, not a need; a browser that is offered a WebP under an AVIF `<source>` sniffs the bytes and shows it); the plates, dark crops and rects for both layouts; the stills; the eight GLBs and the environment map renamed `.glb.wasm` and `.hdr.wasm`, because the host serves no `.glb` or `.hdr` under any type (D0's S2 spike) and three.js's loaders read the bytes, not the name; the cameras and the tints; the manifest rewritten to list only what ships, under the shipped names, with a `phoneSet` note of what was left out; the photographs from `wall/public/zoom/`; the icons. The set: 312 files, 21.0 MB (275 .webp, 11 .js, 9 .wasm, 7 .json, 5 .woff2, 1 .avif, 1 .css, 1 .svg, 1 .png, 1 .ico), in two batches of 255 and 57; the manifest 256 entries of the build's 472. The set went up in two publishes (the tool takes at most 255 files a call) and a third after the review (the page and two renamed chunks, the two old names removed) as **Darkest Shades**: https://claude.ai/artifact/Wwk3W3BUawYqyuvci7m5rt (private; `states.html` is not published, it is the review sheet). **What could not be shown from here:** the VM has no signed-in browser, so the published link answers "Sign in to view this page" to it (as S2's did); the page and its file list were read back through the Artifact tool and match the set (the Artifact tool's file listing shows 313 files, every path of the plan with the page, each under its type: `application/wasm` for the nine renamed files, `image/webp`, `text/javascript`, `font/woff2`, `application/json`, `text/css`; the page read back holds the module script and its three preloads, the inlined stylesheet with its font URLs under `./assets/`, `<drawer-wall>` and the `<noscript>` list, inside the host's own skeleton), and the same set served locally through its `preview.html` (the page inside a copy of the host's skeleton: the doctype, the viewport meta, the host's body reset; written by the tool, never published) passes the wall's flows at 390 px (Playwright as a Pixel 7 at 390 × 844 against `python3 -m http.server` on `work/phone/`: the layout at 390 CSS px in standards mode, the wall's own type on the body and the labels with Urbanist loaded; the wall with its eight labels; `#open-f09-debug` opens the drawer on its last frame; "Lift them out" lifts the live frame at tier 2 (the GLB from `F09.glb.wasm`, the environment from `drawer.hdr.wasm`: `lifted.three` 11 ms, `lifted.glb` 11 ms, the canvas at opacity 1 and 780 × 976 device pixels, progress 1, drawn); "See the photographs" shows the four pictures; no request failed; the four screenshots are committed in `docs/build/drawer-wall/review/R2/` as `r2-wall-390.jpg`, `r2-open-390.jpg`, `r2-lifted-390.jpg` and `r2-photos-390.jpg`). The D7 exit's "the link works from a clean browser at 390 px" is therefore Antaeus's first step on R2's checklist (the Open row), recorded under "Checks failing for environment reasons".

**The switches on the phone link:** an Artifact's link passes a plain `#name` to the page and nothing else (no query string), so the wall reads its switches from the hash as well as the query (`wall/src/lib/flags.ts`): `#pull` (pull first), `#panel` (the records panel), `#debug` (the event log and its copy button), `#open-f09` (a drawer open on its last frame), joined with hyphens for more than one (`#pull-debug`); `?mech=pull`, `?panel=1`, `?debug=1` and `?open=` still work on a plain host and win where both speak. `usability.md` and the device checklist name the hash forms first.

**The two documents, finished:** `docs/build/drawer-wall/usability.md` (the five-person test on their own phones: what to say, the five tasks in order, the table per person, the rule, what to send back; the switches as the phone link takes them; four tasks and no price column since #47, the change below) and `device-checklist.md` (the real-device checklist for R2: open, scroll, tap, pull, buttons, lift, turn, pinch, photographs, smoothness, put back, another drawer, pull first, rotate, low power, weak connection, the records panel, the log; what to send back). Both lost their draft line.

**R2, Antaeus's second look:** the link at the top of this file and in the PR, with what to try (the checklist's rows, in order; then the three questions of the usability test's free play, for himself).

**Found and fixed while building (Nov 9 2026):** (1) **A query string does not pass through an Artifact's link** (only a plain `#name` does, the host's own rule), so `?mech=pull`, `?panel=1`, `?debug=1` and `?open=` would have been dead on the phone link, and the usability test's pull-first start with them; the wall reads the same switches from the hash (`flags.ts`), and the two documents name those forms first. (2) **The host serves no `.glb` or `.hdr`** (D0's S2 spike): the set renames them `.glb.wasm` and `.hdr.wasm` and the manifest it ships names them so; `GLTFLoader` and `HDRLoader` read the bytes and never look at the name, checked by lifting the frame from the set served locally. (3) **Both widths in both formats are 864 sequence files,** over the host's 511 a version: the set ships the 1200 px WebP sequences only (216 files) and the manifest lists only them, so `sequenceWidths()` returns 1200 alone; the player still asks the index for the avif slot and gets the entry's first file, the WebP (`AssetIndex.file(entry, 'avif')`), and the plate's `<source type="image/avif">` names a WebP too, which the browser sniffs and shows. (4) **Vite's preload helper fetched the stylesheet for the view's chunk** (`__vite__mapDeps` listed `preload-helper-*.css`), so the first set, which inlined the stylesheet and carried no CSS file, lost the drawer view to a 404 ("Unable to preload CSS") when served locally; on the Artifact host a stylesheet the host refused would have done the same. The build now puts all CSS in one file linked from the page (`cssCodeSplit: false`), so no chunk carries a CSS dependency, and the set carries the file as well as inlining it. (5) The set carried the states sheet's script; it no longer does. (6) **The first local check was not a 390 px layout** (the D7 review): the stripped page has no doctype or viewport meta (the host adds them), so a phone-emulated browser serving `work/phone` raw laid it out at 980 CSS px and scaled it to 0.4; the tool now writes `preview.html`, the page inside a copy of the host's skeleton, the local check runs through it (390 px, standards mode) and the screenshots above are from that. (7) **Inside the host's skeleton the wall rendered in the system font** (the D7 review, blocks-exit): the host sets `font: 14px -apple-system…` on `body` and the wall's typography sat on `:root` alone, so every element took the host's face and no font file was requested; `base.css` now sets `body { font: inherit }`, the set was rebuilt and republished (Version 3), the local check through `preview.html` reads the text stack and Urbanist loaded on the body and the labels, and `host.spec.ts` serves the built page inside the same skeleton on every run and asserts the type, the 390 px layout and the scene colour. (8) **The shipped manifest failed the wall's own schema** on its `phoneSet` note (the review): the schema now allows the note and the tool validates the shipped manifest against it with the wall's Ajv before writing. (9) **A bare `--out` would have emptied the repository root** (`''` resolved to it before `rmSync`; the review): the tool falls back to `work/phone` and refuses any folder outside `work/`. (10) **The checklist's Pinch row named the right temple for every frame** where F02 carries the emblem on the right wing of the front and F04 and F05 on the right end-piece (the records; the review): the row says so; its Another row no longer promises a cache the wall does not keep. (11) **The switches:** a query value now names its switch both ways (`?mech=tap` beside `#pull` is tap first), and the hash's `open` is documented to take the frame's id only (handles are hyphenated and the hash splits on hyphens; the review).

**The D7 review and its fixes (Nov 9 2026):** four reviewers who did not build the branch read it through the set and the switches as built, the tests and the set as a check, the brand and the documents, and reproducibility; every finding then went to two refuters. ### Change · The lifted frame turns freely (Nov 10 2026)

**The instruction.** After the no-price change merged (PR #19) and Antaeus had opened the phone link, he wrote: "When the drawer opens and the user taps the product, I want their finger to be able to freely manipulate the glasses." The run read it as: once the frame is lifted, one finger turns it about any axis with no limit in any direction, and recorded that as `00-decisions.md` #48, with one open question, O21: whether "freely manipulate" also means moving the frame with two fingers (a pan) and twisting it (a roll). The default builds rotation and zoom only: a roll is reachable by combining turns, and the frame stays centred in the view. Branch `wall/free-turn` from `main` at d8b317a.

**What changed** (`wall/src/`): the turn is a unit quaternion in view space instead of a yaw and a clamped pitch. `lib/gestures.ts` has `TURN_PER_PX` (0.4° a pixel, both directions; `YAW_PER_PX`, `PITCH_PER_PX`, `PITCH_MIN` and `PITCH_MAX` are gone), the pure quaternion helpers (`quatFromAxisAngle`, `quatMultiply`, `quatNormalize`, `rotateVector`), `turnFree(rot, dx, dy)` (a sideways drag turns about the view's vertical, a vertical drag about the view's horizontal, composed on top of the turn so far in view space, so the frame follows the finger whichever way it already faces) and `turnAngles(rot)` (yaw, pitch and roll in degrees, for the tests). `lib/machine.ts`'s context carries `rot` (identity at the inspect pose); `TURN` applies `turnFree`; `RESET`, `RETURNED` and `LEFT` return it to identity. `elements/lifted-frame.ts`'s pose is `{ rot, zoom }`: `applyPose` carries the view-space turn into the world through the camera's rotation (`cam · rot · cam⁻¹`), scales it by the lift's progress (none at the open pose, whole once lifted) and pivots it on the frame's own centre (the GLB's bounds, kept from setup), so the frame turns in place instead of swinging about the model's origin, which the first build did; the zoom moves the frame's origin toward the camera before the pivot is added, so the centre holds under the turn at every zoom (with the zoom after the pivot, as the branch first had it, the centre circled as the frame turned: 52 mm at 3×, 30% of the view's width); and a fit keeps the whole frame in the view: a turn that would carry its temples past the stage's edge moves it back inside, along the camera's up and right, by as much as there is room on the other side and no more (two passes over the box's eight corners, each shift exact for the corner past the edge; whole at 1×, fading to none at 1.25×, since a zoom is a choice to see a part of the frame larger than the view and its anchor must hold). `screenBox()` and `drawCount()` let the tests read where the frame is on the screen and how often it has drawn. `elements/drawer-view.ts` hands `{ rot, zoom }` to the frame and its states-sheet fixture "turned" is the same turn expressed as a quaternion (40° sideways, −10° up). **The finger's turn and the pinch now hand the pose to the frame as the buttons do:** since D5, `onLiftedTurn` and `onLiftedZoom` had dispatched to the machine without that hand-over, so a drag changed the machine's turn while the frame kept its last pose, and leapt to the accumulated turn at the next button press (the review measured a 300 px drag at 390 × 844: `ctx.rot` 120° on, 0 of 1,316,640 pixels changed; then one Tilt down: 86,992 pixels changed, the frame at 165°); every drag and pinch in Versions 1 to 6 behaved so, the e2e tests read the machine's state and passed, and the record's evidence had used the buttons. The buttons and the keys keep D5's steps, Turn left and right and ← → 9.6°, Tilt up and down 8°, ↑ ↓ 2°, now written in degrees and sent as the finger's pixels at 0.4°/px (the branch's first commit had kept the old pixel counts, which at 0.4°/px in both directions made the tilt steps 12.8° and 3.2°, and this record had called the Turn step 24°). The pinch, the double-tap, the wheel, Reset, the inertia (0.92 a frame, none under reduced motion) and the tap that puts the frame back are as they were.

**The tests:** `gestures.test.ts` asserts the constants, that a drag to the right reads as 40° of yaw and a drag down as 40° of pitch, that no direction has a limit (225 px down stands the frame on end, 450 px turns it over, 900 px brings it round, and 1000 px is the same rotation as 100 px), that turns compose in view space (on its end, a drag to the right still turns about the view's vertical), that the quaternion stays unit over 5,000 steps, and the helpers; `machine.test.ts` asserts `TURN` turns freely (400 px down is 160°, past the old clamp, the frame's top pointing down), goes on from where it is, and that `RESET`, `RETURNED` and `LEFT` return the identity; `flows.spec.ts` reads the quaternion from the view (identity when lifted; changed by Turn right, Tilt up and a drag; on the Pixel a 300 px drag down turns the frame past horizontal and a second one keeps turning it) and, in the same read, the live frame's pose and its draw count: the frame holds the machine's turn after every button, drag and pinch, and drew while the finger moved (on the desktop, while the mouse button was down); stood on end by eleven Tilt downs its whole box is inside the view and taller than 60% of it; at 3× (Closer ×7) four Turn rights and seven Tilt downs move its centre by under a pixel; and, for the keyboard, that → swings the frame's forward to the viewer's right and ↑ changes the turn again. `gestures.test.ts` and `machine.test.ts` also drive the tilt the other way (225 and 450 px up; 400 px up) past the old −30° stop. The a11y, perf and states specs are unchanged (the states sheet masks the lifted, turned and zoomed fixtures, so its baselines did not move). Vitest went from 307 tests to 311.

**The documents:** `00-decisions.md` #48 (quoting the instruction; the superseded limit attributed to the plan's Turn row of Nov 6 2026 and D2's code, not to D5) and O21; `DRAWER-WALL.md` step 5 (the pivot and the fit), the Turn row of the interaction constants (the pivot, the fit, the buttons' and keys' steps), the e2e list (what the lift flow asserts), the copy listing (`wall.tiltUp`, `wall.tiltDown`, which step 5 names) and the decision ranges; the folder README's ranges; `device-checklist.md`'s Turn row (any way, no stop in any direction, whole in the view, Reset brings it back; two fingers only pinch, O21). `CLAUDE.md` needed nothing: no non-negotiable changes.

**The review and its fixes (Nov 10 2026):** four reviewers who did not build the branch read it as built in the browser (the rotation math and the frame as it turns, at 390 × 844 and 1440 × 900), as tests and checks, as brand and documents, and for reproducibility; every finding went to two refuters (28 agents). Seventeen findings, twelve verified, eleven stood (three of them the one fact about the button steps), one refuted; the five lighter notes were read by hand. What stood, and what was done: (1) **A finger's drag did not turn the frame on the screen** (it blocked the exit): `onLiftedTurn` and `onLiftedZoom` dispatched to the machine without handing the frame its pose, so a 300 px drag moved `ctx.rot` by 120° and 0 of 1,316,640 pixels, and the next Tilt down made the frame leap 165°; the two lines had been on `main` since D5, and `flows.spec.ts`, reading the machine's state, passed. Both handlers now call `syncLifted()`; the lift flow reads the frame's pose and its draw count in the same call as the machine's state, after every button, drag and pinch; the record's evidence is a finger's drag; Version 7 is published. (2) **At 3× the turn no longer pivoted on the frame's centre** (the zoom ran after the pivot's shift, so the centre circled as the frame turned, 52 mm, 30 to 45% of the view's width): the zoom is applied to the origin before the pivot's shift, and the centre holds to 0.00 px at every zoom (asserted at 3× in the lift flow). (3) **Stood on end the frame was cut flat by the stage's top edge** (from the inspect pose's height the temples reached 93 px above it at 390 × 844): the fit moves the frame back inside by as much as there is room on the other side, whole at 1× and fading to none at 1.25×, where the zoom's anchor holds (asserted in the lift flow; `r2-on-end-390.jpg`); the pivot and the resting height are put to Antaeus in the questions table. (4) **The record's button angles were wrong and the vertical step had grown 1.6× without a decision** (Turn left and right 9.6°, not 24°; Tilt up and down 12.8° where D5 set 8°; ↑ ↓ 3.2° where 2°): the buttons and the keys step in degrees at D5's values, and the record says so. (5) **The known-limits sentence misdescribed the pivot** ("a little behind the bridge", "a few millimetres": it is 79 mm behind, half the frame's depth, and the front recedes about 160 mm over a half turn): rewritten to the measured facts. (6) **#48 attributed the superseded limit to D5** (the plan's Turn row of Nov 6 set it and D2 coded it): the decision and the history note name them. (7) **No test drove the tilt the other way past the old −30° stop:** `gestures.test.ts` and `machine.test.ts` now do. (8) **DRAWER-WALL.md's e2e list still said "turn (yaw changes)" and its copy listing lacked `wall.tiltUp` and `wall.tiltDown`:** both corrected. (9) **"for the tests and the log":** nothing logs the angles; the record and the code comment say "for the tests". (10) **With the drag drawing the frame, the two turn assertions of `perf.spec.ts` failed on this VM** (the median animation-frame gap 33 ms against 17, input to the frame after the next 343 ms against 200): the main thread was idle (0.9 ms a draw, no long task) and the gaps came from Chromium presenting WebGL through SwiftShader, a software renderer, at 80 to 200 ms a frame whatever the canvas (measured with and without antialiasing and alpha, at pixel ratio 1 and 2; the page alone at 60 Hz), which the D6 and D7 figures of 60 fps while turning had never met because the frame was not being drawn. The thresholds stand; the test now names the renderer (`rendererName()`), asserts the wall's own share everywhere (each draw's main-thread time median ≤ 4 ms and max ≤ 16, each pointer event's handlers ≤ 16 ms, one draw per event) and asserts the turn's gaps and latency on a GPU only, recording them otherwise; the row in "Checks failing for environment reasons" says so. Refuted, and left: that the device checklist's Turn row had to state the two-finger assumption (the row sends the founder to O21 already; one sentence was added to it anyway, as the refuters allowed). From the five unverified notes: the pull request pointer was circular (the number is in the Phases row now); `work/phone/` held eight stale Version 4 chunk files beside Version 6's, unlisted and unsent (emptied before the rebuild); the commit trailer names the model (the attribution line the run's instructions set, on every commit of `main`).
