### Change · CI builds the photographs' zoom set (Nov 10 2026)

**What was found.** After PR #23 merged, its CI run failed, and the workflow's history showed that no run had ever passed: 61 runs since D1, every one a failure (the run writing this read 42 of them, the latest twelve and the first thirty; the change's review then read every run's first failed step), which no record section had looked at. The latest runs reached the end-to-end step and failed nine flows on the Pixel and the desktop (the lift flow, the keyboard flow, tier 1, the a11y states and targets), all waiting for "See the photographs": `wall/public/zoom/` is built from the committed stage masters in `dam/product/` by `npm run assets` and is git-ignored by design (D4), so the runner's drawer view had no photographs to offer, as the wall is built to behave without them. With the zoom set built, the end-to-end step passed on the runner (`49 skipped, 68 passed`, the same counts as here) and the Lighthouse step failed at once: the workflow set `CHROME_PATH` to an empty string, which `checks/lighthouse.mjs` handed to the launcher as the browser's path ("The argument 'file' cannot be empty"), so Lighthouse had never completed on the runner: the review of this change read every one of the 61 runs' first failed step, and the fourteen that had reached Lighthouse (runs 1 to 6 and 8 to 14, D1 to D3, and run 37, D5) had all failed at that launch with the same line, from the workflow's first run. The other earlier runs failed before the end-to-end step, at `npm run build` (runs 15 to 28 and 30 to 36, D3 and D4, `main` at 20 and 36: a type error in a unit test, run 15's `TS2352` in `tests/unit/manifest.test.ts`) or at `npm run check` (run 29), and once at the end-to-end step before the photographs' flows existed (run 7, D2, a screenshot protocol error); none was investigated further here, since the same steps pass on the current tree. From run 38 (D5) to run 61, every run failed at the end-to-end step for want of the zoom set.

**What changed:** `.github/workflows/wall.yml`: Python 3.12 (`actions/setup-python@v5`) and Pillow 12.3.0 (the version the VM has), then `npm run assets -- --strict` before the tests and the build, so the runner holds the same zoom set a developer's machine does and the step fails when a photograph is left out; the Lighthouse step pinned to the Playwright Chromium the workflow installs (`CHROME_PATH` from `playwright`'s `executablePath()`), not the image's own Chrome and not the empty string; the zoom set's inputs (`dam/product/**`, the manifest, the export) among the paths that start the workflow. `tools/photo/zoom_export.py`: the product rows only (the manifest's cast rows share a frame and an angle with them, and the last row had won: nine of the 32 photographs carried a portrait's alt text since D4), and `--strict`. Nothing in `wall/` changed; no check or threshold was touched. The plan's D1 deliverable names the zoom step.

**The review and its fixes (Nov 10 2026):** four reviewers who did not make the change read the workflow against the scripts and the export, the record and the plan, for reproducibility, and as the runner would run it; every finding went to two refuters (28 agents). Nineteen findings, twelve verified, ten stood, two refuted; the seven lighter notes were read by hand. What stood, and what was done: (1) **Nine of the 32 zoom photographs carried a cast portrait's alt text and provenance** (since D4: `zoom_export.py` keyed the manifest by frame and angle alone, and a portrait's row, sharing both with a product row, won; a screen reader heard a person who is not in the picture, against CLAUDE.md's "no people in the wall"): the export reads the product rows only (`master_location` `dam/product/`); the index built now carries no cast master. (2) **The CI step could not fail** (the export exits 0 with photographs missing, and the flows open F09 only): `--strict` exits 1 when any photograph is left out, and the workflow passes it. (3) **The workflow's path filters left out the zoom set's inputs:** `dam/product/**`, the manifest and the export are watched. (4) **Lighthouse on the runner used the image's own, unpinned Chrome** (the check's fallback paths are this VM's): the step pins `CHROME_PATH` to the Playwright Chromium the workflow installs. (5) **The record's history of the earlier runs was wrong** (it said the early runs failed before the end-to-end step and that every run had failed for want of the photographs): the review read every run's first failed step; the fourteen that reached Lighthouse (runs 1 to 6, 8 to 14 and 37) failed at the same empty browser path from run 1, 21 failed at the build, one at the check, one at a D2 screenshot, and runs 38 to 61 for want of the photographs; the section, the Phases row, the bullet and the decision row say so. (6) **"a shared two-core machine"** was unsupported (a public repository's runner has four vCPUs): reworded. Refuted, and left: that the pull request pointer "(number below)" resolved to nothing (the number is written in after the pull request is created, as every change's was). The second run after the fixes: run 64 (https://github.com/FastCoempany/darkestshadeswebsite/actions/runs/42782085587), success: `npm run assets -- --strict` in 38 s, Playwright `49 skipped, 68 passed` in 6.8 min, `lighthouse: performance 99, LCP 2262 ms, CLS 0.001, TBT 18 ms` on the Playwright Chromium.

**Exit evidence (Nov 10 2026):** the workflow runs on the branch's pushes: run 63 of the wall workflow, https://github.com/FastCoempany/darkestshadeswebsite/actions/runs/42772629905, conclusion success: `npm run assets` in 35 s, Vitest, the build, the checks, the budget, Playwright `49 skipped, 68 passed` in 5.7 min on the three projects, Lighthouse; 8 min in all (run 62, the branch's first push, had passed the end-to-end step with the same counts and failed at Lighthouse's empty browser path); its Lighthouse line: `lighthouse: performance 99, LCP 2257 ms, CLS 0.001, TBT 58 ms` on the runner's own Chrome; after the review's fixes, run 64 (https://github.com/FastCoempany/darkestshadeswebsite/actions/runs/42782085587), success: the strict photographs step in 38 s, Playwright `49 skipped, 68 passed` in 6.8 min, `lighthouse: performance 99, LCP 2262 ms, CLS 0.001, TBT 18 ms` on the Playwright Chromium the workflow installs.

**Known limits:** the runner presents WebGL through a software renderer, as this VM does, so the turn's frame gaps and latency are recorded there too (the environment table); Lighthouse on the runner is a hosted virtual machine without a GPU (four vCPUs for a public repository's `ubuntu-24.04` runner, by GitHub's specification), so its Total Blocking Time will vary by run as the VM's does, and a failure of that line alone on a run that changed nothing on the load path is noise, to be re-run, never re-thresholded.

### Change · The finger anywhere (Nov 10 2026)

**The report.** After Version 7 was published, Antaeus wrote: "Check version 6 does what you say. From what I'm experiencing, nothing happens when I drag my finger in any direction on the screen after taking the glasses out the drawer. I still see the turn left, right tilt etc buttons." Three checks of the Version 7 phone set ran in the lab (agents that did not build it), each with the set served inside a copy of the host's skeleton: Chromium as a Pixel with touch through CDP, WebKit as an iPhone 14 and 15, and a reading of the whole path from a finger to a redraw.

**What they found.** (1) The published Version 7 is the fixed code: the chunk that handles the drag is byte-identical in the built wall, the local set and the Artifact (read back through the Artifact tool), and its drag and pinch handlers end in `syncLifted()`. (2) Under a finger, Version 7 turns and redraws: on the Pixel a tap on the frame lifted it and seven drags (200 px right, down, up and left, a slow 8.8 s drag, a fast flick, a finger held 600 ms then moved) each changed the machine's turn, handed the same quaternion to the frame, drew it 28 to 40 times and changed 7.6 to 10.3% of the pixels in the glasses' band (one Turn right press: 4.3%); in WebKit (software WebGL, tier 2) every input that reached the handler turned and drew the frame too, though Playwright's WebKit can only tap, so a real iPhone drag stayed unproven. (3) Version 6 reproduces the report exactly: with the one added call removed from the Version 7 chunk in flight, a 150 px drag sent 53 turn events, moved the machine to 79.8° and drew 0 frames, and the next Turn left made the frame leap 70.2°; the buttons show in both versions. A phone that shows the buttons with a dead drag runs the whole of Version 6 from its cache (a half-cached page shows no drawers or opens none). (4) Three gaps in Version 7 itself: only the 4:5 stage listened, so about 40% of a phone's height (the dark room above the stage, the controls' row) was deaf to a drag, and on shorter screens (390 × 664, 390 × 740) the controls sat over the stage's bottom 84 and 46 px, where a drag started on a button and did nothing; a finger that landed while the frame was still rising (`active` false) was ignored for its whole stroke, even after the frame rested; a stroke under 8 px within 400 ms was a tap and put the frame back half a second later (5 and 7 px strokes turned it 2° and were then put back). Untested there, and still: the Claude app's own gestures around the page, the Artifact host's caching, a real phone.

**What changed** (`wall/src/`): `elements/drawer-view.ts` hands the pointer events of its whole screen, the stage's and the dim room's, to `<lifted-frame>` while the frame rises or is lifted (`liftedTarget()`, `pointerDown/Move/Up`, `wheel`), so the finger may start anywhere but the buttons; the controls' row passes the finger through to the room behind it (`pointer-events: none`) and only its buttons take it; a tap on the dim room does nothing. `elements/lifted-frame.ts` binds nothing on its canvas any more (one path, no double handling); its handlers are public and take the element that holds the pointer's capture; a touch begun during the rise is kept, never a tap, and turns the frame from the moment it rests; the tap has its own slop, `isLiftedTap` in `lib/gestures.ts` (`LIFTED_TAP_MAX_PX` 4, a turn of 1.6°, within `TAP_MAX_MS`); a live frame whose setup failed (the GLB, three.js or the WebGL context) dispatches `tier-fallback` with its reason, so the view drops to tier 1 for the rest of the visit and no turn button stands over an inert still (`main.ts` logs the reason). `lib/build.ts` carries the build's commit hash (`vite.config.ts` stamps `__WALL_BUILD__`, the short hash with `-dirty` when the tree had changes), written to the debug log's `start` line and shown in the records panel's head, so a phone can say which build it runs.

**The tests:** `gestures.test.ts` (`isLiftedTap`: 4 px and 400 ms, the drawer's tap keeps 8); `flows.spec.ts`'s lift flow: on the Pixel a drag that starts in the dark room above the stage turns the frame (its pose equals the machine's, its draws rise), a 6 px stroke turns it and leaves it lifted, a finger that lands during the rise and keeps moving turns it once lifted (the pose held); on the desktop a mouse drag beside the stage turns it; a new flow aborts the GLB's fetch and expects the still, tier 1 and no turn button. Vitest went from 311 tests to 312.

**The documents:** `DRAWER-WALL.md` step 5 (anywhere but the buttons; the rise), step 7 (a tap on the drawer behind the frame, under 4 px), the Tap and Turn rows, the e2e list; `device-checklist.md`'s Turn row (start on the glasses, in the dark above, near the buttons, while they rise) and Put back row (a tap on the drawer behind the glasses). `00-decisions.md` #48 stands as written; the finger's reach is the run's reading of it, in the decisions below.

**The phone set and the link:** rebuilt and republished as **Version 8** (the page and the renamed chunks, `drawer-view-tB9_Xr2E.js`, `gestures-CRRsRIbc.js`, `index-C0HZtl5o.js`, `lifted-frame-DZStGuGR.js`, `photo-zoom-Bd4s6fJj.js`, `preload-helper-Dts-5B2P.js`, `records-panel-BPaU1CzJ.js`, `spring-CrFr-wLn.js`, sent; the Version 7 names removed); the debug log's start line now reads `build 2309903`.

**The review and its fixes:** (the review runs after this record is written; its paragraph is added with its findings.)

**Exit evidence (Nov 10 2026):**
- `cd wall && npm run all` → exit 0: `Test Files 13 passed (13)`, `Tests 312 passed (312)`; the build (stamped `2309903`); `strings: 61 files scanned (dist: 23 files), 0 banned strings`, `colors: 32 files scanned, 0 literal colors`, `assets: 472 entries, 930 files listed, 930 files on disk, 0 failures`; `bundle: initial JavaScript 17.90 kB gzipped in 4 files (index-C0HZtl5o.js 1.92 kB, decorate-BRwEpJNf.js 6.07 kB, gestures-CRRsRIbc.js 0.79 kB, preload-helper-Dts-5B2P.js 9.12 kB)`; `bundle: 3D chunk three-CPBoSSGV.js 158.10 kB gzipped …, with lifted-frame-DZStGuGR.js + lifted-three-DWAq_lKn.js 5.11 kB: 163.21 kB for the live frame`; Playwright `50 skipped, 70 passed` on the three projects (two flows more than before: the drag from the dark room and the finger begun during the rise are inside the lift flow; the failed live frame is its own flow, skipped on WebKit); `lighthouse: performance 97, LCP 2258 ms, CLS 0.000, TBT 140 ms`. A first run of the gate on the branch had failed the states sheet's two baselines by 1% of their pixels: the build stamp in the records panel's head had made that row wrap at 390 px and moved every line below it; the stamp moved to a line of its own at the panel's foot (clipped by the sheet's box, and masked), and the baselines were unchanged.
- The flows above in Chromium (the built wall): in the lift flow on the Pixel, a 120 px drag from the dark room 40 px above the stage turned the frame (its pose equal to the machine's, its draw count up); a 6 px stroke in 50 ms turned it and left the state `lifted`; a finger that landed during the rise and moved 1 px every 50 ms until `lifted`, then 160 px more, turned it (the pose held); on the desktop a mouse drag starting 80 px left of the stage turned it; with the GLB's fetch aborted the lift ended at tier 1 with the still shown, `window.__wall.tier` 1 and no Turn left, Tilt up button
- Version 8 published; the link unchanged at the top of this file.

**Known limits:** the Claude app's native gestures (a sheet that pulls down, an edge swipe) and the Artifact host's own frame on a phone are outside the lab; a real iPhone's drag was not driven (Playwright's WebKit taps only); a tap on the drawer behind the lifted frame still puts it back, as the plan has it (a tap in the dark room no longer does); the turn's frame rate on a GPU is the phone's figure (the environment table).

## Copy for sign-off

The `wall` section of `content/copy/en.json`, status `draft`, added in D2. Every string below is Claude's draft in the brand voice and needs Antaeus's yes before launch.

| Key | Draft | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `wall.title` | The frames | The page's only heading, visually hidden |
| `wall.openLabel` | Open the drawer. | Each drawer's accessible name: "{name}. Open the drawer." (no price, #47) |
| `wall.notYet` | Not yet. | A locked drawer's label, in place of the name |
| `wall.soldOut` | Sold out | A sold-out drawer's label |
| `wall.hintPull` | Pull it toward you | The drawer view, shut, after 1.2 s |
| `wall.hintLift` | Tap them to lift them out | The drawer view, open, after 1.2 s |
| `wall.hintTurn` | Turn them. Pinch to come closer. | The lifted view, after 1.2 s |
| `wall.open` / `wall.shut` | Open the drawer / Shut the drawer | The quiet buttons that do what the pull does |
| `wall.close` | Close | Back to the wall |
| `wall.lift` / `wall.putBack` | Lift them out / Put them back | The lift and its reverse |
| `wall.photos` / `wall.photosClose` | See the photographs / Back to the frame | The photographs and back |
| `wall.turnLeft`, `wall.turnRight`, `wall.closer`, `wall.further`, `wall.reset` | Turn left, Turn right, Closer, Further, Reset | The lifted view's buttons |
| `wall.model3dLabel` | {subject}, a view you can turn | The live frame's accessible name |
| `wall.announce.open` | {name}. The drawer is open. | The live region |
| `wall.announce.shut` | The drawer is shut. | The live region |
| `wall.announce.lifted` | {name}, lifted out. | The live region |
| `wall.announce.back` | {name}, back in the drawer. | The live region |
| `wall.announce.photo` | {name}, photograph {n} of {count}: {alt} | The live region, in the photographs (added by the run) |
| `wall.tiltUp`, `wall.tiltDown` | Tilt up, Tilt down | The lifted view's buttons for the vertical drag (added by the run, D5 review) |
| `wall.panUp`, `.panDown`, `.panLeft`, `.panRight` | Up, Down, Left, Right | The photographs' bar while the photograph is larger than the view: the drag's buttons (added by the run, D5 review) |
| `wall.announce.entered` | {name}. The drawer is shut. | The live region when the view opens on the shut drawer (added by the run, D5 review) |
| `wall.panel.title` | Records (example data) | The simulated backend, `?panel=1` (Part 1 names it) |
| `wall.panel.frame`, `.state`, `.light` | Frame, State, Light | The panel's fields (added by the run) |
| `wall.panel.mechanic`, `.tapFirst`, `.pullFirst` | How a drawer opens, Tap first, Pull first | The panel's `?mech=` choice (added by the run) |
| `wall.panel.close` | Close the records | The panel (added by the run) |
